_readme: Vtable layouts for every class with a vtable in DBSIM.EXE and VSHELL.EXE --
applied to the Ghidra project by ES2ApplyVtables.java
(tools/ghidra_scripts/). Re-run that script after adding entries here -- it is idempotent.
The widget family is enumerable rather than discovered one class at a time: Borland emitted a
descriptor record per class, stored 12 bytes before that class's vtable, and it carries the
class's own name. tools/scripts/es2_classes.py --vtables walks both directions, so a new
cockpit control's table is looked up from its class name and a table found in the
disassembly is turned back into a class name. Adding a widget class here is therefore a
matter of naming its instance, not of re-deriving the shape.
This is one of three companion files. known_symbols_<binary>.json owns address->function findings and
known_structs.json owns field layout inside an object. This file owns the SHAPE of a class:
which slot means what, and which addresses hold a table of that shape. A slot's meaning is
recorded once here rather than once per doc that happens to call through it.
Per vtable definition:
name        - Ghidra data-type name, created under category /ES2.
binary      - 'VSHELL' or 'DBSIM' (must match the -process file name at apply time).
description - what the class is; becomes the data type's description.
slots       - ordered, one per 4-byte slot, starting at +0x0 with no gaps. Each has:
name        - the slot's ROLE, not any one class's implementation name.
A slot whose meaning is not established is named
'slot_0xNN' -- never given a guessed role name, so a guess
can never masquerade as a confirmed one (the same rule
known_symbols_<binary>.json applies to low-confidence functions).
description - evidence and the implementations seen in it.
instances   - the addresses holding a table of this shape. Each has an 'address', a 'label'
naming that particular class's table, and a 'description'.
SLOT COUNT IS A FINDING, NOT A GUESS. A table is followed in memory by whatever the linker
put next, and an over-long definition would type that as function pointers -- a fabrication
that reads as confirmed. A definition's length is established by call sites and by what the
trailing words actually are, and the bytes past it are left undefined. A plausible-looking
code address in the word after the last slot is not evidence: two of the tables here hold a
pointer into a class-descriptor record there, which resolves and disassembles like anything
else. Growing a definition later costs nothing; a wrong one has to be noticed first.
ONE CLASS OF TABLE STATES ITS OWN LENGTH. Where a class has a second base -- the cockpit
widgets and REG_OBJ/TS_REG_OBJ are the cases in DBSIM -- the primary table is followed by two
constants, the second of which is the byte offset from the primary table to the mixin's, so
slot count = (constant - 8) / 4. Check for that pair before reasoning from call sites: it is
the binary saying the length rather than the reader inferring it. Its absence means only that
the class is singly inherited.
NO SIGNATURES. Each slot becomes a function definition with the default (undefined) return and
no declared parameters -- the least the shape can claim. Argument
lists are a separate, per-function finding: record one in known_symbols_<binary>.json's 'signature'
field, under the rule stated there, not here.
GENERATED SHAPES. tools/scripts/es2_skeletons.py gives every class record's primary vtable a
shape: its base's when the table is as long as the base's; in DBSIM, a copy of the VSHELL
namesake's when every slot's function has the same name in both binaries; otherwise a new one
whose first slots are its parent shape's. A new slot is named for the role its implementations'
names agree on -- the part after the first '_', less a trailing NoOp or None -- and is
slot_0xNN where they disagree or none is named; its description lists the implementations.
The slot count of such a shape is the run of code pointers up to the next class's type
descriptor.

vtables.name: DrawableVtable
vtables.description: The five-slot interface of DRAWABLE (RTTI, 0xc bytes, no base) and of every class derived from it that adds no virtuals: the transform-only MAT_OBJ, REG_OBJ and TINY_OBJ, their shape-drawing TS_ variants, the TS_OBJ/ANIM_OBJ/DET_ANIM_OBJ chain every shaped simulation object descends from, and the effect classes. SimObjectVtable and ProjectileVtable extend it. FIVE IS ESTABLISHED: in each instance the word after +0x10 is the next block's class-record pointer, the REG_OBJ mixin pair (0xc, 0x1c: (0x1c - 8) / 4 = 5 slots), or data that is not a code address.

slots.name: Draw
slots.description: Draw the object, or for the transform-only classes just install its model transform. DRAWABLE's is pure virtual (Rtl_PureVirtualCalled, 00496684). MAT_OBJ SimObject_InstallModelTransform (00401fe4), REG_OBJ Raster_SetModelTransformFromPose (00401fa8), TINY_OBJ TinyObj_InstallModelTransform (00401f50); the TS_ variants install the transform then draw their shape instance (TSObj_Draw 0046b7e6, TSRegObj_Draw 00402cd4, TSTinyObj_Draw 00402e98); DET_ANIM_OBJ Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel (004033e4); Debris_Draw, Meteor_Render and FlatObj_Draw; LightSource, SMOKE and DummyDrawable install empty bodies.

slots.name: GetPosition
slots.description: A pointer to the object's position triple. DRAWABLE's is pure virtual. MatObj_GetPosition (00402c75) and, from TS_OBJ down, SimObject_GetPosition (0046b801) return this+0x26; RegObj_GetPosition (00402cef) this+0x10; TinyObj_GetPosition (00401f08) a shared static triple. LightSource, SMOKE and DummyDrawable return null.

slots.name: Destructor
slots.description: The deleting destructor, (this, flags), freeing on flags bit 0 -- the function each class record's +0x28 field names.

slots.name: slot_0x0c
slots.description: Stub_ReturnZero (004785bf) in every instance, and in every SimObjectVtable and ProjectileVtable instance. Role not established.

slots.name: GetShapeRadius
slots.description: Drawable_GetRadiusZero (004785c6) until TS_OBJ installs SimObject_GetShapeRadius (0046b80c), which reads the radius off the shape instance.

instances.label: MatObjVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'MAT_OBJ', 0x34 bytes; bases DRAWABLE and Context at +0xc. MatObj_Dtor (0046b97d).

instances.label: TSObjVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'TS_OBJ', 0x41 bytes, derived from MAT_OBJ: the base of every shaped simulation object -- PROJECTILE, EXPLOSION, DEBRIS, SMOKE_BALL, METEOR, FlatObj, FIRE and, through ANIM_OBJ, ACTOR. SimObjectBase_Constructor (00402188) builds it; TSObj_Dtor (0046b890).

instances.label: AnimObjVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'ANIM_OBJ', 0x41 bytes, derived from TS_OBJ. AnimObj_Dtor (00402400) unhooks and frees the shape instance's animation threads.

instances.label: DetAnimObjVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'DET_ANIM_OBJ', 0x45 bytes, derived from ANIM_OBJ; ACTOR's base. Draws with Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel (004033e4); DetAnimObj_Dtor (00426f98).

instances.label: RegObjVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'REG_OBJ', 0x22 bytes; bases DRAWABLE and TSContext at +0xc. RegObj_Dtor (00402e02).

instances.label: TSRegObjVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'TS_REG_OBJ', 0x26 bytes, derived from REG_OBJ; shape instance at +0x22. TSRegObj_Ctor (004020b8), TSRegObj_Dtor (00402cfa).

instances.label: TinyObjVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'TINY_OBJ', 0x16 bytes, derived from DRAWABLE: a two-component position and a heading. TinyObj_Dtor (00402f94).

instances.label: TSTinyObjVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'TS_TINY_OBJ', 0x1a bytes, derived from TINY_OBJ; shape instance at +0x16. TSTinyObj_Ctor (0040201c), TSTinyObj_Dtor (00402eb3).

instances.label: EffectLightVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'LightSource', 0xe bytes, derived from DRAWABLE: an explosion's light handle. EffectLight_Construct (00407604), EffectLight_Destruct (0040765c).

instances.label: ExplosionVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'EXPLOSION', 0x5b bytes, derived from TS_OBJ. Explosion_Construct (00407f1c), Explosion_Destruct (00407e48).

instances.label: DebrisVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'DEBRIS', 0x61 bytes, derived from TS_OBJ. Debris_Construct (00408940), Debris_Dtor (0040f7e6).

instances.label: SmokeVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'SMOKE', 0x2a bytes, derived from DRAWABLE: the emitter, which draws nothing. Smoke_Construct (0040923c), Smoke_Dtor (004096e3).

instances.label: SmokeBallVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'SMOKE_BALL', 0x4c bytes, derived from TS_OBJ. SmokeBall_Construct (00409178), SmokeBall_Dtor (0040970d).

instances.label: MeteorVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'METEOR', 0x59 bytes, derived from TS_OBJ: the drop pod. Meteor_Construct (00409b44), Meteor_Dtor (00424034).

instances.label: FlatObj_Vtable
instances.description: RTTI 'FlatObj', 0x41 bytes, derived from TS_OBJ: a ground shape. FlatObj_Draw (0040991c), FlatObj_Destruct (0041bd46).

instances.label: FireVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'FIRE', 0x5b bytes, derived from TS_OBJ: a burning object's flames. FireEffect_Ctor (0046b388), FireEffect_Dtor (0046b470).

instances.label: DummyDrawableVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'DummyDrawable', 0xc bytes, derived from DRAWABLE; installed by Terrain_FillCellUntextured (0046bb40). DummyDrawable_Dtor (004714e3).

vtables.name: SimObjectVtable
vtables.description: The 34-slot vtable every full simulation object carries -- the base class, the mech class and the flyer class all lay their tables out this way. Its first five slots are DrawableVtable's and its first six ProjectileVtable's, unchanged, so the two hierarchies share a base interface: slots +0x4, +0xc and +0x10 hold the same three functions (SimObject_GetPosition, Stub_ReturnZero and SimObject_GetShapeRadius) in every table in this file. Slot names are the base class's roles; see the individual instances for what overrides what.

slots.name: Draw
slots.description: Draw the object. Base installs Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel (004033e4); the mech overrides with Mech_Draw (004174c8).

slots.name: GetPosition
slots.description: SimObject_GetPosition (0046b801), returning obj+0x26, in every table seen -- base, mech, flyer and all four projectile classes. Scene_SubmitObjectWithRadius (0042837c) and ObjList_DrawCellObjects (00428c60) call it for the object's position.

slots.name: Destructor
slots.description: The deleting destructor, (this, flags): SimObject_Dtor (00427081), Mech_Dtor (00427127), Flyer_Dtor (004271bf), Base_Dtor (00406dab), Base_RadarDtor (00406df3), Base_ArmedDtor (00406d5c), GroundVehicle_Dtor (00406d05), Base_TransportDtor (00406caf). Each counts the RTL destructor counter down once per class level it inlines, runs AnimObj_Dtor (00402400) with flags 0, and on flags bit 0 takes the object off maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList with ObjList_SwapRemove (00411e1c) instead of freeing it.

slots.name: slot_0x0c
slots.description: Stub_ReturnZero (004785bf) in every table seen. Role not established.

slots.name: GetShapeRadius
slots.description: SimObject_GetShapeRadius (0046b80c) in every table -- reads the radius off the instanced shape rather than any type record. See docs/retail/simulation/hit-detection.md.

slots.name: Tick
slots.description: The object's per-tick update. The mech installs Behaviour_DispatchMove (00415afc), which forwards to the current behaviour class rather than moving anything itself; the projectile classes install their own TickUpdate in the same slot. The ACTOR base and the five structure tables install SimObject_TickNoOp (00411ab4), which returns 1.

slots.name: ThinkTick
slots.description: Mech: Behaviour_DispatchThink (00415b38). Second of the three behaviour-class dispatchers; see docs/retail/simulation/ai-dispatch.md.

slots.name: ReassessTick
slots.description: Mech: Behaviour_DispatchReassess (00415b74). Third behaviour-class dispatcher. The five structure tables install Base_ReassessTickNoOp (00406cfe), which returns 0.

slots.name: DirectFireHitTest
slots.description: Hit test AND damage application in one call, offered to each candidate by Sim_RaycastObjectList (00426528). Mech_DirectFireHitTest (00418ba8), Flyer_DirectFireHitTest (00421c8c), Base_DirectFireHitTest (00405038); the ACTOR base's slot is pure virtual (Rtl_PureVirtualCalled, 00496684). See docs/retail/simulation/damage-system.md and hit-detection.md.

slots.name: GetAimNodeTransform
slots.description: The node transform a shot aims at: its +0x14 is the aim point and its +0x1c the sight height. Mech_GetAimNodeTransform (00417b98); base and flyer both install SimObject_GetAimNodeTransform_None (00411a9c), which returns 0 so every caller falls back to the raw origin. See docs/retail/simulation/target-selection.md, 'Aim point'.

slots.name: ReceiveSquadOrder
slots.description: One machine receiving one transmitted squad order; 1 when the order was taken. Mech_ReceiveSquadOrder (00420ad4); the ACTOR base, the flyer and the five structure tables install SimObject_ReceiveSquadOrder_Refuse (00411a64), which returns 0.

slots.name: HandleCommand
slots.description: Mech_HandleCommand (004157c8). The ACTOR base and the structures install SimObject_HandleCommandNoOp (00411a6c), the flyer its own Flyer_HandleCommandNoOp (004215c0); both return 0.

slots.name: GetAimPoint
slots.description: Two out triples: the eye point and the outside view's orbit centre. Mech_GetAimPoint (004155c4); the ACTOR base and the flyer install SimObject_GetAimPointZero (00411a74), the structures Base_GetAimPoint (0040351c).

slots.name: GetShieldByHeading
slots.description: Given a heading, returns the front or rear shield by which side is within +/-90 degrees. Mech_GetShieldByHeading (004154d0); every other table answers SimObject_GetShieldByHeadingZero (00411a4c).

slots.name: GetSpeed
slots.description: How fast the object is travelling, in the units the rest of the simulation quotes distances in. Mech_GetSpeed (00415498), Flyer_GetSpeed (00421584). The ACTOR base and the structures answer SimObject_GetSpeedZero (00411a54), which is why the AI leads a shot at a machine and fires straight at a building.

slots.name: GetTorsoTwistAngle
slots.description: The aim offset the sensor and target-selection arcs are measured from, on top of the heading. Mech_GetTorsoTwistAngle (00415488); Base_GetTurretAngle (00403594) for GUN_BASE and VEHICLE; SimObject_GetTorsoTwistAngleZero (00411a5c) for everything else.

slots.name: GetOverallDamage
slots.description: How far gone the object is, as a Q8 fraction: 0 pristine, 256 destroyed. Mech_GetOverallDamage (00415504). Read by the AI's flee check and the mission-order layer's condition tier.

slots.name: BearingInSensorArc
slots.description: SimObject_BearingInSensorArc (00411acc) in the ACTOR base, the mech and the flyer. All five structure tables override it with Base_BearingInSensorArc_Always (00405308), which answers 1 for any bearing.

slots.name: AiEnemySighted
slots.description: Mech_AiEnemySighted (00412800); every other table installs SimObject_AiEnemySightedNoOp (004127f8). Called out of the detection sweep.

slots.name: CompareCombatRating
slots.description: Mech_CompareCombatRating (0041cabc). Every other table answers SimObject_CompareCombatRatingStub (00411ac0).

slots.name: AiOnTakingFire
slots.description: Called with (attacker, damage) when something hits this object; applies no damage of its own. Mech_AiOnTakingFire (0041f7b8). Base and flyer install Mech_ShareContact (00411aec), which does the contact-sharing half only. See docs/retail/simulation/ai-targeting.md.

slots.name: ComponentNearestAim
slots.description: Which component a shot or a seeker should aim at. Mech_ComponentNearestAim (0041b534); the rocket seeker calls it through the target to fill its steer point (docs/retail/simulation/rockets.md), and a structure's implementation returns its first surviving component (docs/retail/simulation/ai-weapons.md). The ACTOR base and the flyer answer -1 (SimObject_ComponentNearestAim_None, 00411a44).

slots.name: ComponentPosition
slots.description: Places the component ComponentNearestAim chose, in world space. Mech_ComponentPosition (0041b60c), Base_ComponentPosition (00406808). Also the per-component position the explosive falloff measures from. The ACTOR base and the flyer install SimObject_ComponentPositionNoOp (00411a3c), which leaves the out-parameter unwritten.

slots.name: GetBodyRadius
slots.description: Mech_GetBodyRadius (00415518) -- the flat 750 body radius every retail HERC's .DAT states at offset 110. Base_GetBodyRadius (004035a4); SimObject_GetBodyRadiusZero (00411aa4) for the ACTOR base and the flyer. Distinct from GetShapeRadius. See docs/retail/simulation/hit-detection.md, 'The three radius slots'.

slots.name: OnTargetNeutralised
slots.description: Mech_CreditNeutralisedTarget (00415710); every other table installs SimObject_CreditNeutralisedTargetNoOp (00411b2c), an empty body. Called on the ATTACKER by Mech_ComponentDamageWrite when its victim goes out of the fight, carrying the victim and the victim's immobilised reading from before the change -- kill credit and the two squad callouts. See docs/retail/simulation/component-damage.md.

slots.name: AiOnLineOfFireBlocked
slots.description: Mech_AiOnLineOfFireBlocked (0041dd2c): copies the machine's current target position to mech+0x31e and sets mech+0xad. Called from the tail of Sim_RaycastObjectList. Every other table installs SimObject_AiOnLineOfFireBlockedNoOp (00411b34), an empty body. See docs/retail/simulation/ai-combat-states.md.

slots.name: SetRunInto
slots.description: SimObject_SetRunInto (0042200c) in all eight instances, with no override: obj+0xb1 = 1, "something ran into me". Two callers, both collision sweeps naming whatever blocked a move -- Mech_CollisionTest and GroundVehicle_CollisionTest (0046a510), the sweep in StructureGroundVehicleVtable's tick slot. Mech_BehaviourRamTick is the only reader and nothing clears the byte.

slots.name: MissileLockState
slots.description: Mech_MissileLockState (004155ac): returns the per-missile-subtype LOCK flag, NOT an ammunition count. Asked of the launcher: Rocket_Fire will not attach a target without it. Every other table installs SimObject_MissileLockState_Always (00411b04), which returns 1, so a flyer's or a structure's missile always gets the launcher's selected target. See known_symbols_dbsim.json's entry for 004155ac.

slots.name: ApplyExplosiveDamage
slots.description: What an explosion does to this object, called on every object the blast sweep finds in range. Mech_ApplyExplosiveDamage (004187d0); base and flyer share SimObject_ApplyExplosiveDamage (00411b3c). See docs/retail/simulation/damage-system.md, 'Explosive damage'.

slots.name: ComponentDamageWrite
slots.description: The shared component-health write every damage path funnels into. Mech_ComponentDamageWrite (00417de4), Flyer_ComponentDamageWrite (00421bb4); both of the mech's death branches fire the object's defeat action from here. The structures install Base_ApplyDamage (00404d70); the ACTOR base's slot is pure virtual (Rtl_PureVirtualCalled, 00496684).

slots.name: ApplyFormationOffset
slots.description: Places a group member at its formation offset from the leader. Mech_ApplyFormationOffset (00417898); run over every non-leader member by Group_DeploymentCheck for the walk-on arrival verbs. See docs/retail/simulation/mission-deployment.md.

slots.name: GetCollisionRadius
slots.description: This object's half of the collision gap a walking machine measures against it; the mover contributes its own GetBodyRadius. Mech_GetCollisionRadius (0041552c), Base_GetCollisionRadius (004035b8); SimObject_GetCollisionRadiusZero (00411aac) for the ACTOR base and the flyer. See docs/retail/simulation/hit-detection.md, 'The three radius slots'.

slots.name: NextTargetableComponent
slots.description: (this, cursor, int *componentId) -- step a targeting-pod component lock to the next component this object still has, answering the new cursor and writing the component id out. Mech_NextTargetableComponent (00415558) walks a fixed seven-slot rotation, Base_NextTargetableComponent (00403624) walks the structure type's whole component list, and the base class answers -1. The targeting pod is the only caller; see docs/retail/simulation/target-selection.md.

slots.name: ComponentPresent
slots.description: (this, componentId) -- whether this object still has that component, from its occupancy array. Mech_ComponentPresent (00415540), Base_ComponentPresent (0040360c); the base class answers 1 for anything. Asked only by the targeting pod, to notice that the component it had locked has been shot off. See docs/retail/simulation/target-selection.md.

instances.label: SimObjectBaseVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'ACTOR', 0x1f2 bytes: the base class's own table, installed first by Mech_Constructor (00415bb0) at 00415bf4 before the mech's own replaces it at 00415c60. Derived from DET_ANIM_OBJ (004973cc). Most slots hold generic 00411axx stubs; Rtl_PureVirtualCalled (00496684) stands in for the ones a bare object cannot answer.

instances.label: MechVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'MECH', 0x36a bytes: the HERC class. Installed by Mech_Constructor (00415bb0) at 00415c60, after the base table. Overrides 26 of the 34 slots; the table ends at +0x88, where a data block of literals begins.

instances.label: FlyerVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'FLYER', 0x291 bytes: the flyer class. Installed by Flyer_Constructor (004215f4) at 00421624, after the base table. Same 34-slot shape as the base; it is a sibling of the mech rather than a subset -- its objects come from a different pool and are 0x291 bytes to the mech's 0x36a.

instances.label: StructureVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'BASE', 0x209 bytes: the structure base class, and the concrete class for a plain building: BASES.DAT types 0-4, 7, 9, 0x0c-0x1c, 0x1f, 0x21 and 0x24-0x2c. Base_Construct (00405314) installs it FIRST in every one of its five branches and the other four tables then overwrite it, so those four are derived from this one. Its +0x3c returns the shared 00411a5c zero stub -- a plain building has no aim angle -- and Base_Construct sets disarmed (+0xa5) on it at spawn.

instances.label: StructureRadarVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'RADAR_BASE', 0x209 bytes: BASES.DAT types 5, 6, 0x1d and 0x1e. Derived from StructureVtable, and the only slot it overrides is the destructor -- its think and its aim angle are the plain building's. What makes it a radar mast is the construction, not the table: Base_Construct latches scannerActive (+0x96) on, and disarmed (+0xa5) with it.

instances.label: StructureArmedVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'GUN_BASE', 0x220 bytes: BASES.DAT types 8, 0x0b, 0x20 and 0x23, and the parent of StructureGroundVehicleVtable. Derived from StructureVtable. THIS IS THE CLASS THAT AIMS: it replaces the +0x3c zero stub with Base_GetTurretAngle (00403594), which returns the structure's own angle at +0x20f, and its think (Base_ArmedThinkTick, 00404100) maintains the selected-target refcount at +0x1a2. Base_Construct does not set disarmed on it, which is the same conclusion reached from the other direction.

instances.label: StructureGroundVehicleVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'VEHICLE', 0x229 bytes: BASES.DAT types 0x2d-0x3d, the types Base_Construct classifies as targetClass 3 and gives a hit radius of 10 rather than 5. Derived from StructureArmedVtable -- Base_Construct installs StructureVtable, then StructureArmedVtable, then this, and its destructor counts five class levels to the plain building's three -- so it inherits the turret angle and overrides only the destructor and the think (GroundVehicle_ThinkTick, 0046a5d0).

instances.label: StructureTransportVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'LC_BASE', 0x266 bytes: BASES.DAT type 0x22 alone, the TRANSPORT (its MFD name), a landed drop pod with three fixed weapon stations. Derived from StructureVtable, overriding the destructor and the think (Base_TransportThinkTick, 004045c8), which latches disarmed (+0xa5) once every component after the first is at full damage -- so this class starts armed and can lose it, where a plain building is born disarmed. It does not override the aim angle.

vtables.name: ProjectileVtable
vtables.description: The six-slot table the projectile classes carry, and the interface SimObjectVtable's first six slots extend -- which is what lets the draw pass and the raycast walk a projectile and a machine the same way. SIX IS ESTABLISHED, not a floor, on four independent grounds. (1) No code in the class family's own region (0040a100-0040c500: all five constructors, destructors, tick and draw functions) calls any slot above +0x14 on itself. (2) The six CALL dword ptr [reg + 0x18] sites in that region are all the same deleting-destructor call on the MEMBER object at this+0x34, under a null check and with the flag argument 3 -- Bullet_Construct's destructor at 0040b6af and the base's at 0040c38d are byte-for-byte the same sequence -- so +0x18 belongs to that member's class, not this one. (3) The word after +0x14 is not a code pointer in two of the five tables: 00000001 in the bullet's, 00000000 in the beam tracer's. (4) Where it does look like one it is descriptor data -- the base's 0040c3d8 sits inside a class-descriptor record next to the string 'BEAM *', and the rocket's 0046b7c8 at the head of one whose name string is 'TSShapeInstance'; neither address has a function prologue and neither is reached by any call. TS_OBJ (004a0b98), which the projectile base derives from, has five slots -- DrawableVtable's shape -- so +0x14 is PROJECTILE's own addition.

slots.name: Draw
slots.description: Bullet_Draw (0040a120) for the launcher round and the gun round alike; BeamTracer_Draw (0040bc14) for the beam class. See docs/retail/simulation/beam-visuals.md.

slots.name: GetPosition
slots.description: SimObject_GetPosition (0046b801), as in SimObjectVtable.

slots.name: Destructor
slots.description: The deleting destructor: Rocket_Dtor (0040ab8d), Bullet_Dtor (0040b64d), BeamTracer_Dtor (0040ba94), Grenade_Dtor (0040ad2c), ProjectileBase_Dtor (0040c324). Takes a flags argument whose low bit asks it to free the object, which it does through 0047743c.

slots.name: slot_0x0c
slots.description: Stub_ReturnZero (004785bf), as in SimObjectVtable. Role not established.

slots.name: GetShapeRadius
slots.description: SimObject_GetShapeRadius (0046b80c), shared with the full simulation objects.

slots.name: Tick
slots.description: Rocket_TickUpdate (0040a538), Bullet_TickUpdate (0040b124), BeamTracer_LifeTick (0040c2a0), Grenade_TickNoOp (0040acb4). PROJECTILE's own slot is pure virtual (Rtl_PureVirtualCalled, 00496684). See docs/retail/simulation/rockets.md and projectiles.md.

instances.label: ProjectileBaseVtable
instances.description: RTTI 'PROJECTILE', 0x52 bytes, derived from TS_OBJ (DrawableVtable's TSObjVtable, which its destructor ProjectileBase_Dtor reinstalls at 0040c353). vtables.name: CockpitWidgetVtable
vtables.description: The seven-slot table every clickable cockpit widget on the CTLButtonControl branch carries, at object +0x17 -- the offset the class's own Borland descriptor record states, so a widget's primary vtable is always reached the same way. SEVEN IS ESTABLISHED, and on a concrete class the block states it outright: the second of the two constants after the table is the byte offset of the mixin's vtable from the start of the primary one, so slot count = (constant - 8) / 4, and every button class carries 0x24. The three input functions that call through the table fix the slot numbers independently (Widget_OnMouseUp (00452870) reads +0x10 then calls +0x08, Widget_OnMouseDown (004527a0) calls +0x18, Widget_Repaint (00452a90) calls +0x04), and the word at +0x1c is not an eighth slot -- in every table on this branch it is either the next class's descriptor pointer (the [descriptor][0][0][vtable] block header this linker emits), the first of the two constants, or padding. Four of those next-class pointers disassemble as code and would read as a confirmed slot. The slider branch is a separate shape with a genuine +0x1c; see CockpitSliderWidgetVtable. Each class's table is found from its name, and each address here from its table, by tools/scripts/es2_classes.py --vtables, which reads the descriptor record stored 12 bytes before every table. See docs/retail/simulation/cockpit-input.md.

slots.name: Paint
slots.description: Redraw the widget's own content -- re-resolve its caption, pick its frame and colour. Called by slot +0x0c's stage 2, never directly by the input layer. CTLControl's table holds the empty 00452ab2; CTLButtonControl installs 00455545.

slots.name: Invalidate
slots.description: Widget_Repaint (00452a90) calls this and nothing else, so no widget paints inside its own click. The PanelSelectGadget branch installs Widget_InvalidateDeferred (00455524), whose whole body is this->[0x1f] = 2; CTLControl's default (00452ab7) is empty.

slots.name: OnClick

slots.name: FlushDeferredPaint

vtables.name: PanelGadgetMixinVtable
vtables.description: The four-slot table of the PanelGadget mixin -- the second base every concrete cockpit widget carries alongside CTLButtonControl or CTLHSlider/CTLVSlider, and the reason a widget has two vtable pointers. The descriptor records name it: PanelGadget is 8 bytes with its vptr at +0x00, PanelSliderGadget derives from it, and the subobject constant that precedes each table (0x20 for a button, 0x3e for a slider) is where that base sits inside the object -- exactly the amount the table's adjustor thunks subtract. THE MIXIN ADDS NO BEHAVIOUR of its own: three of the four slots thunk straight back into the primary table, and the fourth is the console click. It is not a second interface to implement but the single switch that decides whether a control makes a sound. A class with no mixin table -- CTLControl, CTLButtonControl, CTLSliderControl, CTLHSlider, CTLVSlider, ScrollTrigger, HDDisplayGadget, HDDMapGadget and HUDRovingGunsightGadget -- is silent for want of the base, not for want of an override. The block layout is [descriptor ptr][0][0][primary vtable][subobject offset][mixin vtable offset][this table], and the second constant is that last offset: the distance in bytes from the start of the primary vtable to this one, 0x24 for a button (7 slots * 4 + 8) against 0x28 for a slider (8 * 4 + 8). It holds in all 22 blocks in DBSIM that carry the pair, the two outside the widget family included -- REG_OBJ and TS_REG_OBJ declare a mixin at +0x0c with the constant 0x1c, which is the same arithmetic over a five-slot primary table. The pair is declared by whichever class first mixes the second base in and inherited unchanged by everything below it, so it varies with the branch and not with the leaf. VSHELL's own CTL family carries no such pair anywhere: its widgets are singly inherited and have no mixin. See docs/retail/simulation/cockpit-input.md.

A widget therefore clicks or stays silent according to which of the two mixins it carries, and a class with no mixin at all makes no sound. See docs/retail/simulation/audio.md.
